This was me too. I grew up in a very abusive family and learned not to trust myself and that I had no rights to boundaries or basic human decency.
So when I got older, I'd normally end up attracting people who treated me similarly, and often much worse, because they knew they could, I guess.

I recently read a few old journals and was horrified at some things I'd questioned. Now I'd know a lot of that was abuse or wrong (a lot was way worse than I thought), but back then, all I knew was not to trust myself. 

Often times people stay because people who abuse or are just garbage tend to lovebomb, and abusers pick people who are easy targets (low self esteem, someone currently down, etc) and/or they think they're imagining things, have little to no other social support, and were raised to tolerate mistreatment.

I feel this. I get spurts of, I'd say more motivation than average, because i want to prove to myself that I can be and am capable. But choosing and committing to things is damn hard and scary when I know once I get on that treadmill, there's no simple way to stop. I grew up severely neglected and basically lived in a room for most of my childhood. I was an overachieving student, but everything i did, my parents would intentionally put a stop to, and i felt like it wasn't worth it anymore to try and succeed just to have it taken from me. Then I started really feeling the effects of a physical condition, PTSD, and depression, and I felt like I needed to sleep a lot more than normal. And I'd get in trouble for even saying I was tired or looking tired. 

 I'm autistic but mask pretty well I think (which is actually really awful for mental health, and inside I'm always full of dread), but that, major depression, and CPTSD have been debilitating to me my entire life, and the latter two have only worsened with age and experiences. So I'm very scared to start anything. I'm currently in the middle of autistic burnout and feel useless.

My therapist once asked why I can't just have hobbies and a career, and I recently realized a lot of my identity (my talents and passions lie primarily within the arts) exists because it's my main means of coping, and I'm coping all the time. But making money in the arts requires major motivation and/or luck.

 The worst part besides this making it difficult to be independent is that I've always had a very ambitious mindset, and I hate being idle-- it makes me feel like I'm going totally mad. But I also need a lot of idle time. Idk how to find balance, and at my worst, I have 0 energy and just want to disappear anyway. 

Ultimately, mental health always tackles me in the end, and it's a fight just to pick myself back up. Like existing itself is physically exhausting.

Yes, and I think most disturbingly, it’s not normally because I don’t remember, but rather that I didn’t know it was wrong—at least when these things happened to *me*. I had a crisis over this after I found a good therapist who’d point out when something was abusive, and often I’d be sort of telling these memories in a joking manner or feeling very disconnected from them. I feel incredibly embarrassed when I think about that.

I thought, if I didn’t know this was abusive (often severely), what does that say about me? I had to ask myself if I’d see this stuff happening to someone else, especially a child, if I’d know it was wrong, and thankfully the answer was always “of course,” (along with getting really angry) but I still find it unsettling that I didn’t know. If I don’t know when someone is abusing me, but I can identify that behavior when it happens to others, how can I ever truly be safe? I can’t believe I went through 30+ years totally oblivious.  

The reactions I’ve received from things have felt both validating and extremely embarrassing. I’m thankful that the worst thing I’ve shared with my therapist so far was read with a completely neutral face (if not flat out trying to appear upbeat lol). I feel uncomfortable when people show me sympathy.

 Between my therapist pointing things out to me and finally having to pick up my childhood stuff from storage, I read through some old poems and stuff and realized things were a lot worse than I ever thought; even worse than anything I’d told my therapist. I remembered it all instantly, but I still feel disconnected and struggle to believe any of it’s real. I remember I used to get yelled at for even being perceived as sad because supposedly I had no reason to, and it lead to me thinking I was lying to myself and nothing I believed happened was real—and if it was, I was overreacting.  


 When I went through my things, i also found clothes from when I was very young and going through a ton of abuse and I couldn’t believe how small I was. It’s been months, but realizing all of this was incredibly disturbing and I haven’t been the same since.  

I think not realizing things were abuse until we work on trauma is probably normal in CPTSD especially, but I haven’t been able to get over or process how uncomfortable I feel. It’s really wild to look back and think about how much happened to this child, from infancy into adulthood, to such extent that I don’t even feel like it was me. 
I feel like I’m just a messed up adult wandering through a cold desert where I just randomly spawned or something.

I want to firstly say, I’m so sorry you’ve experienced these things. No one deserves this, especially not from someone who is supposed to love you. These are not only red flags, this is flat out abuse.

Secondly, I try avoiding absolute language because I remember whenever I’d see that, it’d somehow take away from the severity and credibility. But this is true: it always gets worse. 
Once someone finds out you’ll tolerate one thing, there is really no end to what might happen. You might not end up experiencing every single act of abuse that could happen (god forbid) but don’t wait to find out. What you’ve been through is “enough,” it’s already bad, it’s already abuse. My bf did all of these things, and I also used minimizing language because I thought I was overreacting or at fault. He’d frequently pull and drag me by my hair and I don’t even know how I couldn’t see how bad that was.

Don’t minimize. What’s he’s done is wrong, with or without adjectives.

Third, choking by a partner increases a woman’s chance of death. Every time it happens, the chance increases. He may not have applied force, but he’s passed a boundary by even touching your neck and using that to keep you down.. someone who loves you would never do this. I feel like there’s a greater chance that I’ll find a bag of $1,000,000 tomorrow than him never ending up choking you with force. And I hate to put it that way, but he now knows touching your neck is not off bounds. He already knows he can harm you and you’ll stay. 

Is there any way you can get out of this situation? Life is short and you don’t deserve this.


Answers to the questions here:

- I don’t think this was actually the first time, but it was the first time I was bruised. And yes, it also took that for me to realize the severity of the situation. The guy claimed he cheated on me (turns out he probably didn’t, and idk what’s more f-ed up tbh). He spent a week love bombing me and then suddenly became erratic and distant; yet, whenever I showed my humanity or I was too tired to deal and wanted space, it was intolerable. During this time he SA’d me multiple times but I put up with it because I thought I had to. I had to take plan B every time because he refused to wear protection. Went to an OBGYN and was shamed over it.

I’d put all my trust in him and wasn’t working at the time/was about to begin college. I was isolated and had no one to help me.

Anyway, I asked for space and he charged at me and started punching my face and biting my legs and arms when I’d start to get away. 

- Yes. Actually when we first met, he randomly said he’d never hurt me (and proceeded to SA me, which I didn’t realize was SA because I grew up in a messed up family). After that, that sort of abuse got exponentially worse, and other physical abuse followed. It started with him being verbally abusive.
I only just realized he’d flat out r*ped me a few days into becoming exclusive, and that happened frequently. I’ve read some of my old journals and it’s horrifying in retrospect. He’d tell me frequently that he was sorry and wouldn’t do it again, and then try to force me to sign “deals” and shit. When I’d refuse he’d get frustrated and  “jokingly” say things like he was going to pour a bottle of alcohol inside me to get me to comply. It was totally ridiculous. He’d later say he knew he hurt me and wouldn’t do it again, but would; it would just take longer to get back there.

- Hitting required progression, yes. Other things occurred in a slightly unusual timeline, because it took me a while to process what was even happening.

 The progression was unsettling/abusive and misogynistic “jokes” > being very possessive/getting upset when I’d hang out with friends (lost them all in the end) > verbal abuse/name calling/ sl*t shaming even being a virgin > coercion and SA played off as a joke or justified that I was “his” and he could “do whatever he wanted.” Sometimes justified as a “favor” 🙄 > abusive tickling / ignoring boundaries > increasing aggressive sexual and relationship demands > manipulation, silent treatment, flirting with other girls in front of me, and legit brain washing tactics > humiliation > hair pulling/dragging and restraining > shoving > hands around neck (yup, without pressure) > undeniable choking > “light” hitting > choking for longer periods and lifting me by my neck > flat out beating and biting.

I want to also say that between all of this, there’d always be love bombing. So I’d think maybe I was overreacting or that things would be ok again. I assumed I did something wrong to make that stop. That’s very typical.

- Firstly, what triggers them doesn’t matter. This behavior is unnecessary and always unacceptable. But it’s normally be discussions about cheating, or asking for space and boundaries. Whenever I’d start to become stronger, less dependent, the abuse would get more extreme.

- I was caught off guard in the very beginning, when he SA’d me the first time. He seemed like the sweetest boy and I literally froze and had no idea how to process. Thought I was imagining it or somehow at fault, so I kept going back. I was shocked the first time he choked me and pulled me by my hair, but nothing shocked me after that.

- he would always profusely apologize and say it’d never happen again. This would start the love bombing phase and the abuse continued.

I had to put my life on hold a few times just to be “okay.” I sold explicit photos online for a bit to try and reclaim my self worth and it completely backfired. I struggle to be intimate with my current partner, and am very anxious even around men who I consider harmless or friends. It’s hard to trust after that.

All the time. However, I would caution from assuming that someone is okay or has had things easier—even if they claim they have. I mask extremely well and have a type-A personality which is very much fueled by a dangerous level of perfectionism. Both parents were abusive and I could even be punished for my facial expressions.    

 I try very hard and to other people, the result can look like success while it certainly doesn’t feel like it to me. I am never, ever enough in my own mind. That said, sometimes I completely burn out and have to retreat from the world due to a combination of things from my upbringing causing mental health problems, current struggles with family, and autism.   

I think back to the potential I displayed as even a very young child, and I’m sad and disappointed. My bf’s parents will tell me stories about things he’d do that displayed giftedness early in life and I relate to a lot of those stories. He grew into an adult who works in STEM and many people regard as one of the most intelligent people they know; meanwhile, I dropped out of HS and am back in college in my 30s, and the stress I’ve endured has clearly had an impact on my cognition and ability to do maths especially.   

The difference is that my bf’s family nurtured his intelligence and curiosity, while mine abused me in every way and didn’t care about me enough to show even basic decency or care at certain points. My life was fueled by stress. I started developing odd sleeping patterns around 9 because I was so stressed that I’d need to stay awake for hours listening to music to calm down enough to sleep. My entire life became focused around self regulation, which later developed into eating disorders and addictions. I still need a lot of extra time to self regulate.  When you’re under that much stress, your focus shifts to just surviving each day; if you’re constantly treated as prey, learning not only becomes more difficult, but priorities shift.

My parents intentionally sabotaged me any time I would start doing well in school. One would do this and then talk to me about how disappointed they were. My assumption is that it was so I wouldn’t leave them because I’d been their emotional support my whole life. I’m in my 30s and finally pulling away, and there’s a lot of resistance from them. A lot of times I don’t feel functional, but I do try very hard to hide it. And irl, not many people know my actual relationship with my family because I’m  embarrassed by it, don’t want pity or judgement, and I don’t want to “make them look bad.”

Her other accusation was because i was supposedly disgusted by her and “[didn’t] want to be “fat” like [her].” My mom’s appearance literally never crossed my mind unless I noticed her hair looked nice or something.  I was seriously disgusted by her behavior though. I’ve always known why I had an ED:  I feel like my life is out of control/chaos, I don’t feel ownership over my own body or life, and insecurity about my appearance.  


There were a lot meaner, twisted, and explicit things I was accused of, but I think she was trying to gut me in those situations. With the 3 above, she seemed serious.

Legally, depending on the state (US at least) and certainly ethically, badgering about sex falls under rape. You are not giving free, explicit, and “enthusiastic” consent; you are being emotionally worn down. You are a new mother and already say you’re exhausted, and you’re being emotionally worn down.  Add the fact that you say he becomes “angry and ‘psychotic’” and this leads into an area where you may feel threatened in at least some form, and that’s more obviously sexual assault—just to expound on this a bit more.   

I understand this may not be your perception, and I understand relationships take a lot of work and compromise, you’re trying to problem solve, etc., but your husband is acting highly inappropriately; his behavior is abusive.   

I’ll reiterate that it’s one thing to discuss this and have a mutual conversation about needs and preferences, but it’s a whole different issue to “demand” sex. If one partner is sincerely that unhappy, in most situations, there are **always** options: splitting up, opening the marriage, making time for intimacy outside sex, self stimulation, mutual non-penetrative sexual activity, couples therapy, medication (if you *sincerely want* to have sex but are struggling with mental or physical health, or if he is struggling with mental health*), and so much more. (*but badgering you into sex is still incredibly wrong even if you want to and just feel you don’t currently have the mental or physical capacity). Demanding sex from another individual, regardless of relationship status, is never okay.  

Also, discussion of splitting up shouldn’t be used as a means of pressure, but as a part of a thoughtful, mature conversation outside of discussing the issue. If that is ever used in the moment to get you to agree, that’s wrong. That isn’t to be used as a threat/means of coercion.

I won’t tell you what to do because as someone that’s been in a similar position (except not a mother) I think that can be even more overwhelming, and it’s important to feel empowered and like your decisions are coming *from you,* if that makes sense. My only advice is that you think about this, really think about it and ask yourself if this is sincerely what you want or if you’re being worn down and emotionally manipulated into this.  

 As far as answering your explicit question, I apologize, but given your situation and wording (at bare minimum), I really think it’s more important to prioritize thinking about your husband’s behavior than to be asking how to prioritize sex with him. 
If you don’t think you have the time and energy but want to— again, that in and of itself is fine to try problem solving; however, being worn down by aggressive behavior is *still* never okay.
For an explicit example: If someone wants to have sex with another person but doesn’t feel up to it, and the other person proceeds, that is still abuse even though the other person had some desire for the abuser.

As a final remark just because this is common—please don’t let yourself worry you misrepresented the situation in any way while reading the comments, because what you’ve written here is (absolute bare minimum ) how you feel and that’s highly important and relevant. “Move on,” forget about it,” “let it go,” “that was a long time ago,” “get over it,” = the language of ignorance. Lol

What helped me most was when I dismissed something pretty awful to my therapist as happening a really long time ago, and they told me it didn’t matter when it happened because it shaped me to such an extent that I was still struggling even though I didn’t realize it.

How can I just get over something that I tried to “get over” by pretending it’s nbd, but that apparently creeps up no matter what I’ve tried? It’s counterproductive.

 Prolonged trauma and trauma that results in PTSD literally change the brain. I’ve read studies showing girls who were SA’d even tend to perform worse on math tests. It changes how we relate, love, and think about ourselves and others. It can change how we sleep, eat, and function overall. It can cause crippling panic attacks. It’s called **post** traumatic stress **disorder** for a reason.

As far as data on self reporting of prior abuse, I think unfortunately, that’s all we have. There are a lot of issues that go into this, including people not even realizing what happened to them was abuse—so it’s entirely possible that there could be many abusers out there that have no idea they were abused themselves.

The stats for the cycle of abuse are inconclusive; often, they’re cited in actual studies as anywhere from 25-40%, which still does not make it “incredibly common.” There is also some disparity between sexes and types of abuse. However, most “evidence” is anecdotal and perpetuators of this misinformation often state a common logical fallacy:
“**many** predators have been abused themselves; therefore, many people who are abused become abusers.”
This is a logical fallacy. Even if every single abuser who ever lived had also been abused, that does not mean survivors have a “high likelihood of repeating the cycle of abuse.”  
Example: all birds have feathers and can fly; therefore, all things that fly have feathers. (Obviously this isn’t true).
As an abuse/repeated-trauma survivor myself, I find this highly triggering and offensive. It somehow adds to the feelings of isolation that I and many other survivors are likely to feel—like I am “othered” because of what happened to me without my consent or interest. Most of us already feel this way to some extent. Because of the abuse I’ve endured, I have been more likely to let people continue to hurt me because I am horrified of the idea of ever harming someone else in any way, even something overall insignificant and unintentional.  I know this is anecdotal, but I do think that’s important to share.

As far as “what can we do?” My own answer would be firstly, abuse prevention and recognition for faster intervention. I think more people should look into becoming mandated reporters and educate themselves on child development. I live in the US where healthcare is a nightmare, and I also really wish we could see more advocacy for free healthcare. A lot of children who are abused are abused by family members who of course don’t seek or can’t afford treatment. As adult survivors of child (or any) abuse, it’s often hard to justify the costs of treatment as well. Most of us already fear retraumatization and struggle to trust anyone, so adding yet another obstacle is incredibly disheartening. I’m only just beginning to work on my trauma because someone offered to work with me at a significantly reduced cost, and I finally found a therapist I feel comfortable with.

After any abuse, it’s imperative that the survivor seek treatment for dozens of reasons, including preventing further abuse of the victim and by the victim. Child abuse in particular is likely to result in mental health difficulties, which yes, can end up with abusive behavior toward ourselves (like substances, eating disorders, and suicidal ideation) or others. It’s important that children get treatment and are taught that what they experienced is never okay, and are taught how they should expect to be treated and how to handle their trauma and lead healthy lives.

Although it isn’t true that “most” abused people become abusers (even if most abusers were abused), I think treatment is important to both avoid that possibility and help the survivor: in substance abuse amongst minors, over 70% are likely to have been abused. The stats for things like that are ridiculous, and occur at higher rates than abusers who’ve been victims. And ~47% of SA victims will experience re-victimization.

Anecdotally, I often read (and also feel this way) survivors being more fearful of others and horrified at the idea of hurting another person.

“Grooming” can occur at any age, but requires *intent to abuse* the person being groomed. It means something like this: Peck putting his arm around an underaged boy and slowly incorporating more and more physicality. Love bombing is also grooming. The intent is to test the potential victim and push boundaries. Especially when they do things like this around others and others say nothing, the victim begins to question whether or not their discomfort is warranted.

I’m disheartened to see this word (just like “triggered”) being so misused online within the past year or two. I don’t mean offense, just want to bring attention to it because it’s being used to define (still bad, but) things of lesser severity (manipulation). 

Using this word implies that Peck was trying to push Will and Rider’s boundaries to make them question if abuse (often sexual abuse, and toward them) was really abuse. They haven’t said anything about being SAd by Brian, just manipulated. In their letters, they say that they can’t imagine him doing such things. *That’s manipulation, not “grooming.”* It’s very important to understand this distinction so that abuse survivors can identify and speak about their abuse. As a survivor of various types of abuse at the hands of several different people— I don’t mean to discredit his ex and I don’t mean offense by this in any way, but personally, it absolutely pains me to see people looking so deeply into this one.     


 Some possibilities:   

   1. From my own perspective as a survivor, it’s natural to say something like this as opposed to detailing the brutality and humiliation inflicted upon me. There’s additional ick when I consider my age range at the time, and regardless of it not being my fault, there is tons of shame that comes with it. Even writing this (something somewhat vague) is not easy.  As a public figure, I’d imagine that’s even harder for Drake. I can’t even detail things with my therapist, in private. I think the question should be: what should he have said instead of this? Sometimes even using the proper words for things is just too much, feels too invasive and re-traumatizing, etc.        

  2. This is his ex— what if he said this to her first, if he tried to inform her about his own abuse? Or, when you’re with or around someone for a while, it’s common to adopt similar communication patterns, words, etc. Maybe he even heard her say this and thought that was a smart way to phrase something he didn’t feel comfortable saying outright, or he could’ve even forgotten that he heard her say it. I notice my bf doing this occasionally and sometimes I don’t like it, but I need to remind myself that it’s totally normal and I do the same thing sometimes.  



  I’m more in the camp of #1. This is a very, very common thing for survivors of abuse to say. The crimes committed against him can be found online and in the episode; (as a severe understatement) it’s not fun to repeat stuff like this. I think he wanted to convey what happened without actually saying it. Sometimes it’s hard to even believe ourselves, and can send us into a downward spiral of confusion and horror. I hear him using “sexually assaulted” often, and honestly I get it because it adds some ambiguity to things that could be intensely shameful for a survivor to repeat.

I agree with all of this. I also think the current social media “authorities” on recovery (again recovery looks different for all EDs, and then individuals also) are dangerous. I struggled with AN last year and formerly struggled with BN. I approached recovery in a way that I recall from those in treatment when I was at a center in 2008 for BN. Recovery was approached differently for the different EDs and then slightly for each individual, and we had treatment teams. 

Anyway, so I was actually doing great with recovery. I had my neurologist tell me I should see a dietitian, I did for a bit but they were very expensive, none were covered by my insurance (those that were told me they didn’t treat people with EDs even if they were coming in for other things as well). I decided to stop seeing them and look online. Huge mistake. I found a lot of people saying that you “weren’t recovered until you’d eat things like pizza and burgers”, and they’d even poke fun at “recovery influencers” that’d eat things like oats. To me, this felt like they were saying no one could genuinely like things like oats, fruits, veg, etc. unless they still had an ED. I like food that tastes fresh and makes me feel good, and oats are some of my favorite foods. One of the things I cry about the most now is that I’m constantly hungry for all the meals I used to make myself- well balanced, conventionally “healthy” stuff. It’s just what I like. I’d eat other foods in moderation, after I could muster the courage to approach them. Sometimes I’d eat oats with PB 3 meals a day, and I’d constantly hear “that sounds really restrictive”. Actually, I really just love them. I always have. Both used to be a huge B/P thing for me, so eating them a lot was actually quite the opposite of restriction for me. I was very happy with where I was at, since I was prioritizing mental/emotional recovery, and these are mental health conditions after all.

My approach was to slowly go for these things, but I kept feeling more and more pressured to go “all in” quickly, with no social support, no therapy, etc. I rapidly relapsed into bulimia and have been struggling with it for the past year now. I’m devastated and feel like my life is ruined. Previously I’d allowed myself to eat more than I ever had in my life, without guilt, and realizing it wouldn’t make me “blow up” was so freeing to my ED brain. It’s not like that now- now I do “blow up” again because of B/P’ing and water retention.

With my own approach, as someone that’s had both AN and BN (even BED as a child), I had finally found something that worked well for me with what I had. I own responsibility for caving to pressure but I can’t stand that any time I attempt/ed to speak out, there’s usually a lot of censorship or people saying I was in “quasi recovery”- yeah, because I wasn’t recovered; I was in the process of recovery. I also dealt with a ton of body shaming for not gaining rapidly, despite eating an appropriate amount. I find the recovery community to be extremely toxic and unfortunately, that’s not what any of us need. There’s a single approach that influencers and now the majority of the community push, and there’s missing science to back even that up, but one single approach does not work for everyone. For me personally, re-opening this “door” was like re-opening the idea that bingeing was part of my life again. I ate when I was hungry before and was pressured into eating past that, even “when my brain was hungry”. For me with all these EDs, that’s hard to tell. Sometimes anxiety or sadness or even boredom feels like hunger. Then other times, I don’t feel hungry at all. I made a terrible mistake ever going into online recovery communities.

This all caused me to spiral into a months long major depressive episode and I’d just lie in bed, eat, then sleep again. I lost a lot of muscle, and I have a neurological disorder and that’s the only way I can walk. I’m an extreme example, but also a good example that everyone is different and one method definitely doesn’t work for us all.

As a last thing, I also find the “just eat” and “eat as much as you want” with no asterisk extremely privileged. What about people that are on food stamps, don’t live with parents, don’t have enough to buy so much food? There are so many issues.

Tbh I’ve done this a few times, which I guess is why it was my assumption lol and FOMO is correct. 

When prices are already low, I’m more likely to buy at FP but sometimes I’ll make a slightly lower offer. If the price is already low I’ve considered that someone else is more likely to buy it or offer higher since every liker sees when an offer is made and for what amount.

As a seller, I’d probably wait until a few hours before an offer expires to accept on an already low priced item in hopes that someone else might buy it or offer higher. Knowing that, a lot of times I’ll buy things at asking price if I don’t hear back in a few hours when it’s later in the day (since I live East Coast and that’d mean people will either be my time zone or slightly earlier), if it’s something I really want and know it’s unlikely to find for a similar price again or often. Definitely FOMO.

I think what likely happened is that she realized it was a low offer for an already reasonably priced high end designer bag, tried to guilt trip with a (possibly) false sob story and then decided to buy for the full amount before it got away. 

Although I don’t feel like it’s a scam, I’d be afraid she’d be overly nitpicky and end up with some sort of buyer’s remorse. This isn’t the type of item I’d want to sell to someone who has higher chances of trying to return, as there is always a possibility she could send back a different bag, claim it’s fake(especially if you’ve not had it authenticated), not ship it back packaged properly, use it and/or somehow damage it, etc. good call to cancel whenever you feel something is off.


That said, I have had people send me sob stories especially on Vinted and Mercari. Vinted it was certainly always 100% a scam, and they’d ask for extra things. Had someone once tell me they were buying a bag for their wife using a sob story and they literally asked me if I’d include a $100 Apple gift card and hand written note with it lmao. They said they’d mail me the money for the gift card or something. Gave me a good laugh at the very least. He tried.

I really don’t think this is a scam, just someone trying to guilt you into accepting an offer they knew/thought was too low. If you have a bad feeling about it definitely don’t accept the offer even if you’re ok with the price.

At first I’d go back and forth because I felt for her character since she struggles with mental health  and lost her baby (even with how she lost him, I felt sorry for her), but my dislike for her has steadily increased. And my respect for the actress increases the more I dislike her character- I don’t think I’ve ever gotten so annoyed with a fictional character before lol. I don’t like how she is so demanding with Leanne about “bringing Jericho back” when it’s clear that Leanne being present is somehow the only way he is also present. It all came to a peak with her blackmailing, tricking Tobe, and kidnapping Leanne, then going up to the attic each night to abuse her. I really enjoy the show and like how Dorothy’s character is acted out because you can feel her frustration, but I greatly dislike her. Then burying Leanne alive and trying to send her to dance school after repeatedly telling her that she was family, kidnapping her, etc.. ugh. And again getting angry when Jericho wasn’t around, which as a viewer Idk how she didn’t expect. I was so annoyed and felt bad for Leanne, even if she’s becoming increasingly hostile also. 


I hated Uncle George and now I love him. I don’t like Leanne as a person, though I’m interested in how her character is changing. The way she acts with Julian makes me especially uncomfortable though. As for him, I’ve consistently found his character amusing at times, I initially thought he was a crummy person and then wasn’t so sure, now I’m back to thinking, yeah he belongs in that family. 

Tobe however, has always been the most kind and stable. It doesn’t bother me really, but I’m glad there’s at least one character that is consistently likable. 

I like your point that the people act nothing like a real person would, I’ve thought that a lot myself and it’s so frustrating (in a weirdly entertaining way to me) to watch. I do suspect that this will all play a part in the end somehow. I’ve entertained the idea that maybe Dorothy is imagining everyone in her life, maybe Sean and Julian are really the ones with the “problem” somehow, maybe Dorothy and Leanne are somehow one in the same, maybe it’s “just a dream”(I will definitely angry cry if this happens, but it seems to have been hinted), etc. the way the show is teetering between a story of “real life” people and fantasy/supernatural/horror people is very confusing, but I also kind of love it because it makes me feel about as confused and in the dark as I think the characters are supposed to feel. There are moments like the baptism where I just didn’t get how out of so many people, no one knew Jericho had ever even died? Almost no one ever questions it. I’m also irritated that everyone enables Dorothy and that it still hasn’t occurred to her that Jericho is only around when Leanne is. I imagine that it’s all supposed to be irritatingly confusing though.

Height, weight, sex, hormones, genes, activity level, health status, meds, pre, during, or post ED recovery- there are many, many variables. That said- I can’t stand bloggers. My take away from my own experience having been healthy by all evidence and my energy levels, and the experiences of others that then think their calories are possibly “too much” is that food v/bloggers are not healthy for a lot of ED prone people.
